scenes.title: The plan

scenes.title: Key ideas
items: Pay out a share of expected income, not headline (e.g. 70%).
Retain the rest as a loss buffer; it absorbs the losses you assumed in 13.2.
Pay from the T0/T1 ladder (Module 12.4), refilled by income, so payouts never depend on…
scenes.vo: First, Pay out a share of expected income, not headline (for example 70%). Next, Retain the rest as a loss buffer; it absorbs the losses you assumed in 13.2. Then, Pay from the T0/T1 ladder (Module 12.4), refilled by income, so payouts never depend on selling anything that day. Also, never pay from principal. If income falls short, the payout falls. And finally, Review quarterly: if realised income is below expected for two quarters, cut the payout to 70% of the new realised level.

scenes.title: Worked example
steps: If a position fails as assumed, the buffer absorbs it and the payout…
scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. Expected income $23,300 a year times 70% = $16,310 a year paid out ($1,359 a month). $6,990 a year retained. If a position fails as assumed, the buffer absorbs it and the payout continues.

scenes.title: Checklist
items: Payout ratio written (≤ 70–80% of expected income)
Paid from the ladder, not from positions
scenes.vo: Here's your checklist. Do it now, for real. First, Payout ratio written (at most 70 to 80% of expected income). Next, Paid from the ladder, not from positions. Then, Quarterly review rule written. And finally, "Never from principal" rule written.
